title: GAP Claims Desk Time Limits Card
content:
# GAP Claims Desk Time Limits Card — Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda

Every claim under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda runs on five calendar-day limits fixed per waiver. Each count runs in calendar days from the event that starts it, which is day 0.

| Waiver | Claim reported after the insurer's settlement date (days) | Documents supplied after the claim is reported (days) | Stolen vehicle unrecovered before a theft claim is paid (days) | Approved benefit paid after the last document (days) | New evidence after a denial (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kessler GAP Waiver 125 | 90 | 60 | 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Kessler GAP Used Vehicle 140 | 90 | 60 | 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Kessler GAP Waiver 150 | 90 | 60 | 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Kessler GAP Plus 150 | 120 | 90 | 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Kessler GAP Plus 175 | 120 | 90 | 30 | 30 | 60 |
| Kessler GAP Commercial 130 | 60 | 45 | 30 | 30 | 60 |

## What each limit counts

- **Claim notice** — calendar days after the primary insurer's settlement date within which the claim must be reported.
- **Claim documents** — calendar days after the claim is reported within which the required documents must be supplied.
- **Theft waiting period** — calendar days a stolen vehicle must remain unrecovered before a theft claim is paid.
- **Claim payment** — calendar days after the last required document within which an approved benefit is paid.
- **Denial appeal** — calendar days after a denial within which the holder may submit new evidence for review.

## Counting example (hypothetical dates)

A Kessler GAP Commercial 130 claim whose insurer settlement is dated Day 0 has a 60-day notice limit: a report on Day 60 is in time, a report on Day 61 is not. The same settlement under a Kessler GAP Plus 150 leaves the report in time through Day 120.
